========================================
Céline Dion fans prepare for comeback concert in Paris Céline Dion greeted fans today as she left her hotel, hours before she kicked off her comeback concert in Paris. The Canadian singer returns to the stage on Saturday for her first full concert in six years, to open a sell-out Paris residency after a battle with a rare neurological disorder put a pause in her career. Some fans arrived as early as 06:00 to get a spot in front of LeRoyal Monceau hotel to catch a glimpse of the star before she left. She is one of the best-selling music artists of all time and is due to perform a series of 26 concerts over the next eight months. item.title: How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance
item.description:
【原文链接】：https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cy5z02w1zxxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss
========================================
How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance Fighters from the Iran-backed Houthi group have seized territory close to the Bab al-Mandab Strait in the Red Sea - a key trade gateway that links Asia and Europe. Houthis have said they pose no threat to international shipping but have reiterated their intention to target vessels from Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. At least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week, according to the United Nations. BBC Verify's Thomas Copeland reports. Produced by Aisha Sembhi. Graphics by Mark Edwards. item.title: Has Trump won over voters with his midterm convention?

Has Trump won over voters with his midterm convention? Republicans gathered in Dallas for the closing day of the party's first-ever convention held in the middle of a US presidential term, where US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance spoke to voters. The aim of the convention was to boost enthusiasm among supporters, even as protesters of Trump gathered outside. The BBC's North America editor Sarah Smith breaks down the main takeaways from the two day event. item.title: Watch: Americans remember what they were doing on 9/11
item.description:

Watch: Americans remember what they were doing on 9/11 On Tuesday 11 September 2001, hijackers seized US passenger jets and crashed them into two New York skyscrapers, killing thousands of people. A third plane destroyed the western face of the Pentagon - the giant headquarters of the US military just outside the nation's capital, Washington DC. The fourth plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back. It is thought the hijackers had meant to attack Washington's Capitol Building. The BBC spoke to Americans in Washington about what they were doing on that day and how 9/11 has changed the country. item.title: Brother of Muslim police cadet killed in 9/11 'disappointed' by calls for Mamdani to sit out memorial
item.description:

Brother of Muslim police cadet killed in 9/11 'disappointed' by calls for Mamdani to sit out memorial This year’s 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks has become embroiled in divisive politics. There are controversial calls for the city’s first Muslim Mayor to sit out the commemorative event, including from Rudy Giuliani who was New York’s mayor on the morning of 9/11. Mayor Zohran Mamdani has said he will attend and his focus will be on the families who lost loved ones. Zeshan Hamdani lost his older brother Salman, a Muslim American New York police cadet, in the North Tower. He spoke to the BBC's Nada Tawfik over his thoughts on this anniversary. Drone display recreates the Twin Towers over New York City According to organisers, 2,977 drones recreated the Twin Towers at full scale with each light representing a victim of the 9/11 attacks. The artwork, titled "2,977 Lights Over New York Harbor", is a commemorative public art installation in collaboration with artists, producers, and members of the 9/11 community, including victims' families, survivors, and first responders.
